questions.q: Why does Harbor Point Support use Public Read Only on Case, rather than Private like Meridian's Opportunities?
options: Agents don't own a fixed set of customers — any agent may need to see any case to help someone
Public Read Only is always the correct OWD for Case
Private OWD is not supported on the Case object
Public Read Only automatically grants write access too
questions.explain: The OWD follows the business shape: shared, unowned queue work needs broader read visibility than individual sales territories do.

questions.q: What is a queue, functionally, in this lesson's model?
options: A report that lists all open cases
A type of sharing rule
A special kind of public group that holds unowned records until a member claims one
A field-level security setting
questions.explain: A queue acts like a public group — any member can pick up a case sitting in it, rather than the case starting pre-assigned to an individual.

questions.q: Why does Harbor Point use a case team for escalation instead of simply reassigning the case to Tier 2?
options: Reassignment is not technically possible on Case records
Case teams are required by Salesforce for all support processes
Case teams are faster to configure than reassignment
Reassigning loses the original agent's context; a case team keeps them visible while the new tier takes over ownership
questions.explain: Adding the next tier to the case team (rather than reassigning) preserves the prior agent's access and history instead of erasing it.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the criteria-based sharing rule for Priority = Critical in this design?
options: It hides critical cases from Tier 1 agents
It grants the Tier 3 queue write access to critical cases immediately, in parallel with normal escalation
It deletes resolved critical cases automatically
It changes the OWD for just critical cases
questions.explain: The rule gets Tier 3 engineering access to critical cases right away rather than waiting for a manual escalation step.

questions.q: The lesson's check-yourself question asks what would have to change if Harbor Point handled sensitive data requiring tier-restricted read access. What does that imply about Public Read Only as a default?
options: It's a design choice tied to this scenario's shared-queue model, not a universal service-org default
Public Read Only is appropriate for every service org regardless of data sensitivity
Sensitive data cannot be stored in Salesforce under any OWD
Public Read Only would need to be replaced by Public Read/Write
questions.explain: The lesson frames OWD as following the business's actual access needs — a more restrictive scenario would call for a different starting OWD and added narrowing tools.
